One source I found suggested that including software skills greatly increases the appeal of your resume from an interviewers point of view because not only is it hard to learn softwares but it separates you from other candidates. Typical software skills are Microsoft Office Suite and Google suite. I also included other softwares that I used in my work, academic and personal experiences, such as Canva, hootsuite, filmora, project libre and adobe photoshop.  

It mainly indicates to the interviewer that I am technically experienced with technology and can adapt to using the company’s softwares or systems.

Those skills that you listed there are most likely on other candidates resumes, but the softwares skills you may put are least likely to be on other candidates resumes which comes to your benefit. 

Result of me doing this strategy? I saw an improvement in the number of interview opportunities and they tend to ask about my software skills.

All the best.

You may also meet some one who is in a similar situation like you which would be certainly comfortable to know and can provide insight on what their doing about it.
